k > 4. The breakthrough work of Keating and Snaith [KS00b], based on analogies with
random matrix theory, produced the following very general conjecture.

after.text:
The main idea behind the Keating and Snaith conjecture was to model ζ(s) by the char-
acteristic polynomial of random unitary matrices. Denote by 1/2 + itn the non-trivial zeros
of ζ(s). Under RH, it follows that tn ∈ R. The motivation behind the Keating-Snaith con-
jecture stands in Montgomery’s conjecture [Mon73] that the two-point correlations between
the heights tn of the non-trivial zeros of ζ(s), as n → ∞, are the same as those between the
eigenvalues of random complex hermitian matrices as the size of the matrix goes to infinity.

neighboring_unit_entries.title: Arithmetic truncation and Gaussian log-values predict the same moment exponent
neighboring_unit_entries.why_material: Derives the k^2 logarithmic exponent from two distinct representations: divisor-coefficient diagonal sums and a Gaussian model for log|ζ|, while isolating an arithmetic Euler factor from an unknown global factor.

neighboring_unit_entries.title: Match zero density to matrix size, then restore prime arithmetic
neighboring_unit_entries.why_material: Explains the transfer from GUE/CUE zero statistics to characteristic-polynomial moments via N≈log(T/2π), identifies what random matrices recover, and notes that the arithmetic factor must be supplied or recovered by hybrid models.

related_synthesis_entries.claim: Diagonal divisor sums supply the prime Euler factor a_k, while characteristic-polynomial moments supply the global Barnes-G factor g_k; hybrid models are needed to recover both.
related_synthesis_entries.limit: This is a conjectural asymptotic architecture for higher moments, not a proof of the full constants.
related_synthesis_entries.title: Arithmetic and random-matrix factors are complementary, not interchangeable
